answers.solution:
Solution written to **`~/git-prepare-commit-msg-substring-dedupe.md`** (356 lines). All commands in it were executed and verified on git 2.53.0 in throwaway repos.

## Root cause
Two identical substring bugs, which is why the defect hides:

1. **Guard:** `grep -q "Co-authored-by: <Name>"` matches the string anywhere on any line, so prose that quotes the trailer makes the hook `exit 0` and skip the real trailer.
2. **Verifier:** `grep -c 'Co-authored-by: <Name>'` counts that same prose line and reports `1` — a false pass. SUT and test share one blind spot.

A third trap: `grep -E` treats `+` as a quantifier, so an address like `<email>` won't match its own literal pattern. Use `grep -F`.

## The fix (recommended hook)
```sh
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
msg_file=$1
trailer='Co-authored-by: Ada Lovelace <<email>>'

if git interpret-trailers --parse "$msg_file" | grep -qxF "$trailer"; then
  exit 0
fi
git interpret-trailers --in-place --if-exists addIfDifferent \
  --trailer "$trailer" "$msg_file"
```
- `interpret-trailers --parse` sees only Git-recognized trailers (the trailer block), not prose.
- `grep -qxF` = whole-line, fixed-string equality (no substring, no regex metachar issues).
- `--if-exists addIfDifferent` is duplicate defense-in-depth.
- Minimum alternative if Git is too old: `grep -qxF "$trailer" "$msg_file"`.

## Verified results
The regression script in §4.2 produced exactly one canonical trailer for all four cases (normal, mid-line prose, final-paragraph prose, already-trailered):
```
commit 1 exact-trailer count: 1
commit 2 exact-trailer count: 1
commit 3 exact-trailer count: 1
commit 4 exact-trailer count: 1
PASS: all commits carry exactly one canonical trailer
```

The writeup also covers message-side discipline (don't put the literal trailer in prose), an exact-count history audit, consent-gated amend + `--force-with-lease` (verified tree-identical), and a tree-identical `git commit-tree` remedy on a side branch for shared mains (verified same tree, same patch, trailer present).

signatures.description: A prepare-commit-msg hook that guarantees a co-author trailer on every commit with an idempotence guard `if grep -q "Co-authored-by: <Name>" "$MSG_FILE"; then exit 0; fi` is defeated by PROSE: any commit message that merely mentions the trailer string anywhere in its body makes the grep match, so the hook exits 0 and the commit ships WITHOUT the mandated standalone trailer line. Hit live 2026-11-03 on terminal-jail commit af8caf3 (foreman evidence commit whose message cited the trailer string while auditing trailer counts): exact-line count `git log -1 --format=%B | grep -cxE 'Co-authored-by: <Name> <email>'` = 0 while substring count = 1 (the prose line). Subtle trap: a naive verification `git log -1 --format=%B | grep -c 'Co-authored-by: <Name>'` returns 1 (matching the prose) and reads as a FALSE PASS. Fix directions: (1) make the presence check line-anchored (`grep -cxE '^Co-authored-by: <Name> <email>$'`) or use `git interpret-trailers --parse`; (2) keep the full trailer string OUT of commit-message prose (say 'co-author trailer' instead) — message-side discipline alone prevents the skip; (3) verify trailers with an exact-line count, never a substring grep. For an already-pushed trailer-less commit the only real fix is amend+force-push (consent-gated on shared mains) — otherwise file the defect and stage a tree-identical message-fixed remedy commit on a side branch.
